title: Studying in Scotland as an International Student
excerpt: Scotland offers world-ranked universities, lower costs than London and the same visa rules. See cities, tuition, living costs and work options for 2027.

Why Choose Scotland?

Scotland combines historic universities, friendly cities and a lower cost of living than London. International students follow the same UK Student visa rules as in England, so the visa process is identical.

  • Strong universities: Edinburgh, Glasgow, St Andrews, Aberdeen and Strathclyde are well known internationally.
  • Four-year bachelor's degrees: more time to explore subjects before specializing.
  • Lower living costs: rent and daily costs are usually below London in most Scottish cities.
  • Safe, welcoming cities: large international student communities.

Tuition and Living Costs

International tuition differs by university and subject. As a rough range, expect about £14,000 to £28,000 per year, with medicine and some lab-based degrees higher. Confirm fees for your specific course.

For a Student visa, maintenance funds are the same across the UK outside London: £1,171 per month now, rising to £1,203 from 30 November 2026. Scottish cities use this lower rate. For nine months that is about £10,539 now and £10,827 after the rise.

Scholarships and Work Options

Many Scottish universities offer international scholarships, and some are automatic discounts on tuition. Look for them during application. While studying, you can usually work up to 20 hours a week in term time.

💡
After graduationThe Graduate Route is a UK-wide visa. For applications from 1 January 2027, it lasts 18 months. Scotland also has no separate student visa, so you can switch to a Skilled Worker role anywhere in the UK if eligible.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Scotland cheaper than England for international students?
Living costs are often lower outside Edinburgh, and a four-year bachelor's means one more year of tuition. Compare total cost, not only yearly fees.
Do I need a different visa for Scotland?
No. You apply for the same UK Student visa as for any other UK university.
Can I work in England after studying in Scotland?
Yes. The Graduate Route and Skilled Worker visas apply across the whole UK.
